Each symptom lasts 5–60 minutes and symptoms occur in succession. Headache usually follows within an hour but aura may occur alone, especially in older people. Hemiplegic migraine (motor aura) and migraine with brainstem aura are distinct subtypes.
det.diagnosis: Diagnosis is clinical using ICHD-3 criteria: at least two attacks with typical fully reversible aura that spreads gradually and lasts 5–60 minutes. Red flags requiring imaging and vascular work-up include first aura after 50, sudden onset, motor or prolonged aura, aura always on the same side, or a changing pattern. Distinguish from TIA (sudden, negative, simultaneous symptoms), focal seizures (faster spread, brief) and CAA spells in the elderly.
det.treatment: Acute treatment uses NSAIDs or paracetamol, with triptans taken at headache onset rather than during aura; gepants and lasmiditan are alternatives when triptans are contraindicated. Preventive options include propranolol, amitriptyline, topiramate, flunarizine, candesartan, CGRP monoclonal antibodies and, for chronic migraine, botulinum toxin. Oestrogen-containing contraception should be avoided in women with aura. Address smoking and other vascular risk factors.
det.prognosis: Attacks often lessen with age, and isolated aura without headache becomes more frequent later in life.
pearls: Positive phenomena that spread slowly = aura; sudden negative deficits = TIA.
Combined oral contraceptives are contraindicated in migraine with aura.
Persistent aura beyond an hour needs imaging for migrainous infarction.
det.thd: ไมเกรนชนิดมีอาการนำ (aura) เกิดจาก cortical spreading depolarisation ที่ค่อย ๆ ลามไปบนผิวสมอง จึงทำให้อาการค่อย ๆ ขยาย เช่น เห็นแสงหยัก ๆ หรือชาลามจากมือขึ้นหน้า นาน 5–60 นาที แล้วตามด้วยปวดศีรษะ วินิจฉัยจากประวัติตาม ICHD-3 แต่ต้องตรวจเพิ่มถ้า aura เริ่มหลังอายุ 50 ปี เกิดทันที หรือมีอ่อนแรง รักษาเฉียบพลันด้วย NSAIDs หรือ triptan ป้องกันด้วยยา เช่น propranolol, topiramate, flunarizine และควรเลี่ยงยาคุมที่มี estrogen

name: Hypoglycaemia
formal: Low blood glucose causing adrenergic symptoms and neuroglycopenia — confusion, seizures, coma or focal deficits that can mimic stroke; reversible with prompt glucose.
simple: Very low blood sugar, which can cause sweating, confusion, fits or even stroke-like weakness; it gets better quickly with sugar.
th: น้ำตาลในเลือดต่ำ — สับสน ชัก หมดสติ หรืออ่อนแรงครึ่งซีกคล้าย stroke แก้ด้วยกลูโคส
feat: Sweating, tremor, palpitations, hunger, then confusion
Focal deficit that resolves with glucose
Insulin, sulphonylurea, alcohol, liver failure, insulinoma
inv: Capillary glucose in every acute neurological presentation

case.who: 74-year-old man on insulin and a sulphonylurea
case.story: Found confused and weak on the left side at 6 a.m.; he skipped dinner the night before.
case.exam: Sweaty, GCS 13, left arm and leg 3/5, extensor left plantar.
case.tests: Capillary glucose 1.9 mmol/L; deficit resolves within 15 minutes of IV dextrose. CT brain normal.
case.q: Why must glucose be checked before any stroke reperfusion decision?
case.a: Hypoglycaemia can mimic a focal stroke exactly and is corrected in minutes; treating it as stroke would be harmful.

det.patho: The brain depends almost entirely on glucose; when blood glucose falls (usually below about 3.0 mmol/L or 54 mg/dL) adrenergic counter-regulation produces warning symptoms, and further falls cause neuroglycopenia. Most cases occur in people with diabetes on insulin or sulfonylureas; other causes are alcohol, liver or renal failure, sepsis, adrenal insufficiency and insulinoma. Repeated episodes blunt the warning response (impaired awareness).
det.clinical: Autonomic symptoms — sweating, tremor, palpitations, hunger, anxiety — precede confusion, odd behaviour, slurred speech, seizures and coma. Focal deficits, including hemiparesis that resolves with glucose, can closely mimic stroke. Elderly patients and those on beta-blockers may have no warning. Prolonged severe hypoglycaemia can cause permanent damage to the hippocampus, basal ganglia and cortex.
det.diagnosis: Check capillary glucose immediately in any acute neurological presentation and confirm with a laboratory sample. Whipple's triad — symptoms, low glucose, relief with glucose — supports the diagnosis in non-diabetic patients. In unexplained cases, draw insulin, C-peptide, proinsulin, beta-hydroxybutyrate and a sulfonylurea screen during the episode. MRI after severe events may show DWI changes in cortex, hippocampi or internal capsule, sometimes reversible.
det.treatment: Give oral glucose if the patient is alert and can swallow; otherwise IV dextrose (for example 10% dextrose 150–200 mL or 50% dextrose 50 mL) or IM glucagon. Give thiamine first in malnourished or alcohol-dependent patients. Sulfonylurea-related hypoglycaemia can recur for many hours, so observe and consider octreotide. Review diabetes medications and educate on prevention.
det.prognosis: Rapid correction usually leads to full recovery; prolonged coma carries a risk of lasting cognitive impairment.
pearls: No stroke code should proceed without a glucose result.
Sulfonylurea hypoglycaemia is prolonged — admit and monitor.
Thiamine before or with glucose in at-risk patients prevents Wernicke encephalopathy.
det.thd: น้ำตาลในเลือดต่ำ (ประมาณ <3.0 mmol/L หรือ 54 mg/dL) ทำให้สมองขาดพลังงาน เริ่มจากใจสั่น เหงื่อออก มือสั่น หิว แล้วสับสน ชัก หมดสติ และอาจอ่อนแรงครึ่งซีกคล้าย stroke สาเหตุพบบ่อยคือยาเบาหวาน เช่น insulin และ sulfonylurea ต้องเจาะน้ำตาลปลายนิ้วในผู้ป่วยระบบประสาทเฉียบพลันทุกราย รักษาด้วยกลูโคสทางปากหรือ dextrose ทางหลอดเลือด ให้ thiamine ในผู้ที่ดื่มสุราหรือขาดอาหาร และเฝ้าระวังนานในรายที่เกิดจาก sulfonylurea

name: Pituitary apoplexy
formal: Acute haemorrhage or infarction of a pituitary adenoma causing sudden headache, visual loss, ophthalmoplegia and acute hypopituitarism.
simple: Sudden bleeding into a pituitary tumour, causing a very bad headache, loss of vision and double vision, and dangerous hormone deficiency.
th: เลือดออกในเนื้องอกต่อมใต้สมองเฉียบพลัน — ปวดศีรษะรุนแรง ตามัว เห็นภาพซ้อน ขาดฮอร์โมนเฉียบพลัน
feat: Thunderclap headache with bitemporal field loss or acuity drop
Third, fourth or sixth nerve palsy (cavernous sinus)
Adrenal crisis — give hydrocortisone
inv: MRI pituitary; cortisol and pituitary hormone panel

case.story: Sudden severe frontal headache while watching television, then vomiting and blurred vision.
case.exam: Bitemporal field loss, right ptosis with a dilated pupil and limited adduction, BP 88/50.
case.tests: MRI: haemorrhagic sellar mass extending into the right cavernous sinus; random cortisol low; sodium 128 mmol/L.
case.q: What must be given before anything else?
case.a: Intravenous hydrocortisone for acute adrenal insufficiency; then urgent neurosurgical and endocrine review.

det.patho: Sudden haemorrhage or infarction within a pituitary adenoma — often previously undiagnosed — causes rapid expansion of the sellar contents. Pressure spreads upward to the chiasm and laterally into the cavernous sinuses, while destruction of normal gland causes acute hypopituitarism. Precipitants include anticoagulation, surgery, pituitary stimulation tests, pregnancy, dopamine agonists and hypertension.
det.clinical: Abrupt severe headache, often thunderclap, with nausea and vomiting is typical. Visual loss (bitemporal field defects or reduced acuity) and ophthalmoplegia from III, IV or VI palsies follow; the third nerve is most often affected. Meningism and reduced consciousness may occur from blood in the subarachnoid space. Acute ACTH deficiency causes hypotension, hyponatraemia and collapse, which can be fatal if missed.
det.diagnosis: MRI of the pituitary is the investigation of choice, showing a sellar mass with haemorrhage; CT may miss it. Take blood for cortisol, thyroid function, prolactin, gonadotrophins, electrolytes and glucose, but do not delay steroid treatment for results. Formal visual acuity and fields guide management. SAH, CVT, meningitis and basilar artery thrombosis are the main mimics.
det.treatment: Give IV hydrocortisone (100 mg bolus then ongoing replacement) promptly to all suspected cases, along with fluid resuscitation. Management is shared between neurosurgery, endocrinology and ophthalmology. Patients with severe or deteriorating visual loss or reduced consciousness usually undergo early transsphenoidal decompression; milder cases may be managed conservatively with close monitoring. Long-term hormone replacement is frequently needed.
det.prognosis: Ophthalmoplegia usually recovers; visual field outcome depends on severity and duration of compression, and many patients need lifelong hormone therapy.
pearls: Thunderclap headache + ophthalmoplegia + visual loss = image the sella.
Give hydrocortisone before any test results return.
CT can look normal; MRI is needed.
det.thd: เลือดออกหรือขาดเลือดเฉียบพลันในเนื้องอกต่อมใต้สมอง ทำให้ก้อนขยายเร็ว กด optic chiasm และ cavernous sinus อาการคือปวดศีรษะรุนแรงทันที ตามัว ลานสายตาผิดปกติ และเห็นภาพซ้อนจากเส้นประสาท III, IV, VI อ่อนแรง ร่วมกับขาด cortisol เฉียบพลันซึ่งอันตรายถึงชีวิต วินิจฉัยด้วย MRI ต่อมใต้สมอง ต้องให้ hydrocortisone ทางหลอดเลือดทันที แล้วพิจารณาผ่าตัดผ่านทางจมูกถ้าการมองเห็นแย่ลง

name: Paroxysmal hemicrania
formal: Trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia with frequent short attacks (2–30 minutes, many per day) of strictly unilateral orbital pain with ipsilateral autonomic features, completely responsive to indomethacin.
simple: Many short daily attacks of severe one-sided eye pain with a watery eye or runny nose, which stop completely with the drug indomethacin.
th: ปวดรอบตาข้างเดียวเป็นช่วงสั้น ๆ หลายครั้งต่อวัน ร่วมกับน้ำตาน้ำมูกไหล หายได้ด้วย indomethacin
feat: Attacks 2–30 min, often >5 per day
Absolute response to indomethacin
inv: MRI with pituitary views

case.story: Up to 15 attacks a day of stabbing pain around the left eye lasting about 10 minutes, with a watery red eye and blocked nostril.
case.exam: Normal between attacks.
case.tests: MRI brain with pituitary views normal; attacks stop completely within two days of indomethacin.
case.q: Which feature separates this from cluster headache?
case.a: Shorter, more frequent attacks and a complete response to indomethacin.

ddx.pt: Longer attacks (15–180 min), fewer per day, no indomethacin response
Seconds-long shocks with triggers

aN: chronic paroxysmal hemicrania | cph | episodic paroxysmal hemicrania

det.patho: A trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia in which activation of the trigeminal–autonomic reflex produces unilateral pain with cranial parasympathetic outflow; the posterior hypothalamus is implicated as with cluster headache. It is rare, slightly more common in women, and usually begins in adulthood. Secondary forms from pituitary or posterior fossa lesions are described.
det.clinical: Attacks of severe, strictly one-sided orbital, supraorbital or temporal pain last about 2–30 minutes and recur several to many times a day. Ipsilateral tearing, eye redness, nasal congestion, ptosis or miosis accompany the pain, and patients may be restless. Some attacks can be triggered by neck movements or pressure. Episodic and chronic forms exist depending on remission periods.
det.diagnosis: Diagnosis follows ICHD-3 criteria and requires a complete response to therapeutic doses of indomethacin. A trial typically escalates oral indomethacin from 25 mg three times daily up to 75 mg three times daily over 1–2 weeks. MRI with attention to the pituitary is recommended because secondary causes exist. Differentiate from cluster headache, SUNCT/SUNA and hemicrania continua.
det.treatment: Indomethacin is both diagnostic and therapeutic, titrated to the lowest effective dose, with gastric protection. Alternatives for intolerance include COX-2 inhibitors, topiramate, verapamil and occipital nerve blocks, but none are as reliable. Periodic attempts at dose reduction are reasonable in episodic forms.
det.prognosis: Benign course with excellent control on indomethacin; long-term gastrointestinal and renal side effects need monitoring.
pearls: Short, frequent, one-sided attacks with autonomic signs = try indomethacin.
Failure of an adequate indomethacin trial argues against the diagnosis.
det.thd: Paroxysmal hemicrania เป็นปวดศีรษะกลุ่ม trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia ปวดรุนแรงรอบตาข้างเดียวครั้งละ 2–30 นาที เกิดหลายครั้งต่อวัน ร่วมกับน้ำตาไหล ตาแดง คัดจมูกข้างเดียวกัน ลักษณะสำคัญคือหายสนิทด้วย indomethacin ซึ่งใช้ทั้งวินิจฉัยและรักษา ควรทำ MRI ดูต่อมใต้สมองเพื่อหาสาเหตุแฝง และแยกจาก cluster headache ที่ปวดนานกว่าและไม่ตอบสนองต่อ indomethacin

name: Syncope
formal: Transient loss of consciousness due to global cerebral hypoperfusion, with rapid onset, short duration and spontaneous complete recovery; reflex (vasovagal), orthostatic or cardiac in origin.
simple: A faint: brief loss of consciousness because not enough blood reaches the brain, followed by quick full recovery.
th: เป็นลมหมดสติชั่วคราวจากเลือดไปเลี้ยงสมองไม่พอ ฟื้นเร็วและสมบูรณ์
feat: Prodrome of light-headedness, sweating, greying vision; triggers like standing, pain, micturition
Brief myoclonic jerks can occur (convulsive syncope) but recovery is quick
Exertional or supine syncope suggests a cardiac cause
inv: ECG; lying/standing BP; echo or rhythm monitoring if cardiac features

case.story: During a blood draw she felt hot, nauseated and grey at the edges of vision, then slumped; bystanders saw a few jerks of the arms for 5 seconds.
case.exam: Fully alert within a minute; normal examination; ECG normal.
case.tests: Lying/standing BP normal.
case.q: Do the jerks make this an epileptic seizure?
case.a: No — brief myoclonic jerks are common in reflex syncope; the trigger, prodrome and quick full recovery point to syncope.

ddx.pt: Aura, automatisms, prolonged post-ictal confusion
Long events with eyes closed, fluctuating movements

aN: faint | vasovagal syncope | reflex syncope | convulsive syncope | cardiac syncope

det.patho: Transient global cerebral hypoperfusion — systolic pressure falling to roughly 50–60 mmHg for several seconds — causes loss of consciousness and tone. Reflex (vasovagal, situational, carotid sinus) syncope arises from inappropriate vasodilatation and/or bradycardia; orthostatic syncope reflects autonomic failure, hypovolaemia or drugs; cardiac syncope results from arrhythmia or structural heart disease and carries the worst prognosis.
det.clinical: Reflex syncope typically follows prolonged standing, pain, emotion, micturition or coughing, with a prodrome of warmth, nausea, sweating and fading vision. Loss of consciousness lasts seconds to under a minute, with pallor and rapid reorientation. Brief irregular jerks occur in many fainters and are often mistaken for seizure. Syncope during exertion, while supine, with palpitations or a family history of sudden death suggests a cardiac cause.
det.diagnosis: A detailed eyewitness history plus examination, lying and standing BP and a 12-lead ECG resolve most cases. High-risk ECG features include conduction block, long or short QT, Brugada pattern, pre-excitation and ischaemia. Further tests are chosen by suspicion: echocardiography, ambulatory or implantable loop monitoring, tilt-table testing and carotid sinus massage. EEG and brain imaging are not routinely helpful. Features against syncope include prolonged post-ictal confusion, lateral tongue biting and head turning.
det.treatment: Reflex syncope is managed with explanation, trigger avoidance, hydration, counter-pressure manoeuvres and, rarely, medication or pacing for cardioinhibitory forms. Orthostatic hypotension responds to stopping offending drugs, fluids and salt, compression garments, and midodrine or fludrocortisone. Cardiac syncope requires treating the underlying arrhythmia or structural disease, including pacemakers or ICDs.
det.prognosis: Reflex syncope is benign apart from injury; cardiac syncope carries a substantially increased mortality.
pearls: Jerks during a faint do not mean epilepsy — ask about prodrome and recovery speed.
Exertional syncope is cardiac until proven otherwise.
Every patient with transient loss of consciousness needs an ECG.
det.thd: Syncope คือหมดสติชั่วคราวจากเลือดไปเลี้ยงสมองไม่พอ ฟื้นเร็วและสมบูรณ์ แบ่งเป็น reflex (vasovagal) จากความดันต่ำตามท่า และจากหัวใจซึ่งอันตรายที่สุด มักมีอาการนำ เช่น หน้ามืด เหงื่อออก คลื่นไส้ อาจมีกระตุกสั้น ๆ ได้แต่ฟื้นไว ไม่สับสนนาน การวินิจฉัยอาศัยประวัติจากผู้เห็นเหตุการณ์ วัดความดันท่านอนและยืน และ ECG ทุกราย ถ้าเป็นลมขณะออกแรงหรือขณะนอนให้นึกถึงสาเหตุจากหัวใจ

name: Leptomeningeal metastases
formal: Spread of cancer cells to the leptomeninges and CSF, producing multifocal deficits — cranial neuropathies, radiculopathies, headache, hydrocephalus and encephalopathy.
simple: Cancer that has spread to the fluid and linings around the brain and spinal cord, causing several nerve problems at once.
th: มะเร็งกระจายไปที่เยื่อหุ้มสมองและน้ำไขสันหลัง — เส้นประสาทสมองและรากประสาทเสียหลายตำแหน่ง
feat: Multiple cranial nerve palsies and radicular pain/weakness at different levels
Breast, lung, melanoma and haematological cancers
inv: MRI brain and spine with contrast: leptomeningeal enhancement
Large-volume CSF cytology (repeat if negative)

case.story: Over 3 weeks: headache, double vision, numb chin on the right and pain radiating down the left leg.
case.exam: Left sixth nerve palsy, right mental nerve sensory loss, absent left ankle jerk.
case.tests: MRI: linear enhancement of the cauda equina roots and basal meninges; CSF protein high, glucose low, malignant cells on the second sample.
case.q: Why is a single negative CSF cytology not reassuring?
case.a: Sensitivity of one sample is limited; repeated large-volume samples are often needed.

aN: carcinomatous meningitis | leptomeningeal carcinomatosis | neoplastic meningitis

det.patho: Tumour cells reach the subarachnoid space by haematogenous spread, direct extension from brain or epidural deposits, or along nerves, and then disseminate through the CSF to coat the brain, spinal cord, cranial nerves and roots. Breast cancer, lung cancer (particularly EGFR- or ALK-driven adenocarcinoma) and melanoma are the leading solid tumours; leukaemia and lymphoma also seed the meninges. Obstruction of CSF flow causes communicating hydrocephalus.
det.clinical: The defining feature is involvement of several levels of the neuraxis at once: headache, confusion, multiple cranial nerve palsies (diplopia, facial weakness, hearing loss), radicular pain, cauda equina symptoms and asymmetric lower motor neuron leg weakness. Raised pressure causes nausea and altered consciousness. Symptoms usually evolve over weeks, often in patients with known advanced cancer but occasionally as the first sign.
det.diagnosis: Gadolinium-enhanced MRI of the whole brain and spine should precede LP and shows nodular or linear enhancement of sulci, cranial nerves, cerebellar folia or cauda equina roots. CSF typically has raised opening pressure, high protein, low glucose and lymphocytes; malignant cells on cytology confirm the diagnosis but sensitivity of a single sample is modest, so repeat large-volume samples. Circulating tumour cell assays and cell-free tumour DNA in CSF improve detection. Infections, sarcoidosis and post-procedural enhancement are mimics.
det.treatment: Treatment is palliative and individualised: focal radiotherapy to symptomatic sites, proton craniospinal irradiation in selected patients, intrathecal chemotherapy (for example methotrexate or cytarabine via an Ommaya reservoir) and systemic targeted or immune therapies that penetrate the CNS. CSF diversion relieves hydrocephalus. Steroids, analgesia and early palliative care are central.
det.prognosis: Median survival is usually measured in months, though patients with targetable tumours responding to therapy can survive longer.
pearls: Several cranial nerve and root deficits at different levels = think leptomeningeal disease.
Image before LP, and repeat CSF cytology if the first is negative.
det.thd: มะเร็งกระจายไปยังเยื่อหุ้มสมองชั้นในและน้ำไขสันหลัง พบบ่อยในมะเร็งเต้านม ปอด melanoma และมะเร็งเม็ดเลือด อาการเด่นคือมีปัญหาหลายตำแหน่งพร้อมกัน เช่น ปวดศีรษะ สับสน เส้นประสาทสมองหลายเส้นอ่อนแรง ปวดตามรากประสาท และขาอ่อนแรง วินิจฉัยด้วย MRI สมองและไขสันหลังฉีดสี และตรวจเซลล์มะเร็งในน้ำไขสันหลังซ้ำหลายครั้ง การรักษาเป็นแบบประคับประคอง ได้แก่ ฉายรังสี ยาเคมีบำบัดเข้าน้ำไขสันหลัง ยามุ่งเป้า และการระบายน้ำไขสันหลัง

name: Tabes dorsalis
formal: Late neurosyphilis affecting the dorsal roots and dorsal columns, producing lightning pains, sensory ataxia with Romberg sign, areflexia, Argyll Robertson pupils and Charcot joints.
simple: A late stage of untreated syphilis that damages the sensory pathways of the spinal cord, causing stabbing pains, unsteady walking in the dark and odd pupils.
th: ซิฟิลิสระยะท้ายทำลายรากประสาทรับความรู้สึกและ dorsal column — ปวดแปลบ เดินเซในที่มืด รูม่านตาผิดปกติ
feat: Lightning pains, sensory ataxia, positive Romberg
Argyll Robertson pupils (accommodate but do not react to light)
Areflexia, bladder dysfunction, Charcot arthropathy
inv: Serum treponemal and non-treponemal tests; CSF VDRL

case.story: Years of sudden stabbing leg pains and now falling when washing his face in the shower.
case.exam: Small irregular pupils that constrict to near targets but not to light, absent ankle and knee jerks, loss of joint position sense, Romberg positive, painless swollen right knee.
case.tests: Treponemal test positive; CSF VDRL positive with raised protein.
case.q: Name the pupil abnormality.
case.a: Argyll Robertson pupils — light–near dissociation.

ddx.pt: UMN signs plus low B12; no pupillary signs

det.patho: A late form of neurosyphilis appearing years to decades after untreated Treponema pallidum infection, in which inflammation of the dorsal roots near their entry zone leads to degeneration of the dorsal columns. Loss of proprioceptive and pain afferents underlies the ataxia, areflexia, neuropathic joints and painless ulcers. It is now uncommon but persists where syphilis remains untreated and in people with HIV.
det.clinical: Lightning pains — brief, stabbing pains in the legs — and visceral crises are characteristic. Sensory ataxia causes a wide-based stamping gait that worsens in the dark, with a positive Romberg sign. Examination shows areflexia, loss of vibration and joint position sense, hypotonia, and Argyll Robertson pupils (small, irregular, light-near dissociation). Bladder dysfunction, impotence, Charcot joints and optic atrophy may follow.
det.diagnosis: Serum treponemal tests are positive in almost all cases, whereas non-treponemal tests (RPR/VDRL) may be negative in late disease. CSF shows lymphocytic pleocytosis and raised protein in active disease; a reactive CSF VDRL is specific but insensitive. Test for HIV. Differentiate from B12 deficiency, copper deficiency, diabetic pseudotabes and sensory neuronopathies.
det.treatment: Neurosyphilis is treated with IV aqueous penicillin G (18–24 million units daily) for 10–14 days; ceftriaxone is an alternative in penicillin allergy where desensitisation is not possible. Repeat CSF examination monitors response, especially in HIV. Lightning pains respond to neuropathic pain agents such as gabapentinoids or carbamazepine. Physiotherapy and joint protection help function.
det.prognosis: Treatment halts progression, but established dorsal column damage and pain often persist.
pearls: Argyll Robertson pupil: accommodates but does not react to light.
Romberg positive + areflexia + lightning pains = dorsal roots and columns.
Non-treponemal serology may be negative in late syphilis — use a treponemal test.
det.thd: Tabes dorsalis เป็นซิฟิลิสระบบประสาทระยะท้าย เกิดการอักเสบของรากประสาทรับความรู้สึกด้านหลังทำให้ dorsal column เสื่อม อาการคือปวดแปลบแบบฟ้าผ่าที่ขา เดินเซโดยเฉพาะในที่มืด Romberg บวก รีเฟล็กซ์หาย และรูม่านตาแบบ Argyll Robertson ตรวจเลือดด้วย treponemal test (ในระยะท้าย RPR อาจเป็นลบ) และเจาะน้ำไขสันหลัง รักษาด้วย penicillin G ทางหลอดเลือด 10–14 วัน และควรตรวจ HIV ร่วม

name: Botulism
formal: Presynaptic neuromuscular blockade by Clostridium botulinum toxin causing acute descending paralysis beginning with cranial nerves, with dilated poorly reactive pupils and autonomic features.
simple: Poisoning from a bacterial toxin (often from badly preserved food) that blocks nerve signals to muscles, starting with the eyes and face and moving down the body.
th: พิษโบทูลินัม — อัมพาตไล่จากศีรษะลงล่าง หนังตาตก เห็นภาพซ้อน รูม่านตาขยาย มักเกิดจากอาหารหมักดอง/หน่อไม้ปี๊บ
feat: Descending paralysis: ptosis, diplopia, dysphagia then limbs and respiration
Dilated unreactive pupils, dry mouth, constipation
Clusters after home-canned food (e.g. bamboo shoots)
inv: Clinical; toxin assay in serum/stool/food
EMG: small CMAPs with post-tetanic facilitation

case.story: A day after sharing home-canned bamboo shoots, all developed blurred and double vision, dry mouth and difficulty swallowing; one is now short of breath.
case.exam: Bilateral ptosis, fixed dilated pupils, facial and neck weakness, symmetric arm weakness, normal sensation.
case.tests: FVC falling; toxin sent from serum and leftover food.
case.q: What is the key treatment and why give it early?
case.a: Botulinum antitoxin — it neutralises circulating toxin but cannot reverse toxin already bound, so it limits progression.

ddx.pt: Pupils spared, fluctuating, AChR antibody
Ataxia and areflexia with GQ1b antibody; pupils usually normal
Ascending with sensory symptoms and high CSF protein

aN: botulinum toxin poisoning | food borne botulism | wound botulism | infant botulism

det.patho: Botulinum neurotoxin, produced by Clostridium botulinum, binds cholinergic nerve terminals and cleaves SNARE proteins needed for acetylcholine release, blocking neuromuscular and autonomic cholinergic transmission. Exposure routes include ingestion of preformed toxin in poorly preserved food (in Thailand, home-canned bamboo shoots have caused outbreaks), wound contamination (notably injecting drug use), infant intestinal colonisation and iatrogenic overdose of cosmetic or therapeutic toxin. Recovery requires sprouting of new nerve terminals.
det.clinical: Symptoms begin hours to days after exposure with blurred vision, diplopia, ptosis, dysarthria and dysphagia, then symmetric descending weakness of neck, arms, respiratory muscles and legs. Pupils are often dilated and sluggish, with dry mouth, constipation and urinary retention. Consciousness and sensation are preserved and fever is absent. Respiratory failure can develop rapidly. Food-borne cases often appear in clusters.
det.diagnosis: Treatment decisions are made on clinical grounds. Confirmation is by mouse bioassay or newer assays for toxin in serum, stool, gastric contents or food, and by culture. Nerve conduction shows low CMAP amplitudes with facilitation at high-frequency stimulation, normal sensory responses; repetitive stimulation may be normal early. Distinguish from Miller Fisher syndrome and pharyngeal–cervical–brachial GBS, myasthenic crisis, tick paralysis and brainstem stroke.
det.treatment: Give antitoxin (equine heptavalent) as early as possible on clinical suspicion, as it neutralises only circulating toxin and does not reverse established paralysis. Monitor vital capacity and admit to ICU early; many patients need prolonged mechanical ventilation. Wound botulism also needs debridement and antibiotics; aminoglycosides should be avoided because they can worsen neuromuscular blockade. Notify public health to trace the source and other exposed people. Infant botulism is treated with human-derived botulism immune globulin.
det.prognosis: With modern intensive care mortality is low, but recovery takes weeks to months as new terminals form.
pearls: Descending paralysis + dilated pupils + clear mind + no fever = botulism.
Give antitoxin on clinical suspicion; do not wait for lab confirmation.
Clusters after shared home-preserved food are a public health emergency.
det.thd: Botulism เกิดจากสารพิษของเชื้อ Clostridium botulinum ที่ยับยั้งการหลั่ง acetylcholine ที่ปลายประสาท พบได้จากอาหารที่ถนอมไม่ถูกวิธี เช่น หน่อไม้ปี๊บ บาดแผล หรือการฉีดสารพิษเกินขนาด อาการคืออ่อนแรงไล่จากศีรษะลงล่าง หนังตาตก เห็นภาพซ้อน กลืนลำบาก รูม่านตาขยาย ปากแห้ง แต่รู้สึกตัวดีและไม่มีไข้ วินิจฉัยจากอาการเป็นหลักร่วมกับตรวจหาสารพิษ ให้ antitoxin โดยเร็วที่สุด เฝ้าระวังการหายใจใน ICU และแจ้งหน่วยงานสาธารณสุข

name: Thyroid eye disease
formal: Autoimmune orbitopathy, usually with Graves disease, causing extraocular muscle enlargement with restrictive ophthalmoplegia, proptosis, lid retraction and risk of compressive optic neuropathy.
simple: Swelling of the eye muscles from thyroid autoimmunity, causing bulging eyes, retracted eyelids and double vision.
th: โรคตาจากไทรอยด์ — ตาโปน หนังตาดึงรั้ง เห็นภาพซ้อนจากกล้ามเนื้อตาบวมแข็ง
feat: Lid retraction and lid lag (not ptosis)
Restrictive upgaze/abduction limitation; inferior and medial rectus most affected
Watch for colour vision loss (optic nerve compression)
inv: Thyroid function and TSH-receptor antibodies
CT/MRI orbits: muscle belly enlargement with tendon sparing

case.story: Gritty eyes and vertical double vision worst in the morning, now worse looking up.
case.exam: Bilateral lid retraction and proptosis, restricted upgaze of the right eye, normal pupils, no ptosis.
case.tests: TSH-receptor antibodies high; orbital CT: enlarged inferior and medial recti with tendon sparing.
case.q: Why is the upgaze limited?
case.a: The tight, swollen inferior rectus restricts the eye from moving upward (restrictive, not paretic).

ddx.pt: Fatigable ptosis, no proptosis; both can coexist

aN: graves ophthalmopathy | graves orbitopathy | thyroid orbitopathy | ted | dysthyroid eye disease

det.patho: Autoantibodies against the TSH receptor and IGF-1 receptor on orbital fibroblasts drive inflammation, glycosaminoglycan deposition and adipogenesis, enlarging the extraocular muscles and orbital fat. It mostly accompanies Graves disease but can occur in euthyroid or hypothyroid patients. Smoking is the strongest modifiable risk factor, and radioiodine can worsen active disease.
det.clinical: Features include lid retraction and lag, proptosis, gritty eyes, periorbital swelling, conjunctival injection and restrictive diplopia. The inferior and medial recti are enlarged most, so upgaze and abduction are limited. Disease follows an active inflammatory phase of months to two years, then a stable fibrotic phase. Compressive optic neuropathy at the orbital apex — reduced acuity, colour desaturation, field loss, RAPD — is the sight-threatening complication.
det.diagnosis: The diagnosis is clinical, supported by thyroid function and TSH-receptor antibodies. CT or MRI orbits shows fusiform enlargement of muscle bellies with tendon sparing. Activity is graded with the Clinical Activity Score and severity with EUGOGO criteria. Exclude orbital myositis, lymphoma, carotid–cavernous fistula and myasthenia, which can coexist with thyroid disease.
det.treatment: All patients should stop smoking, achieve stable euthyroidism and use lubricants; selenium helps mild disease in selenium-deficient regions. Active moderate-to-severe disease is treated with IV methylprednisolone pulses, with options such as mycophenolate, tocilizumab, orbital radiotherapy or teprotumumab (an IGF-1R antibody). Compressive optic neuropathy requires urgent high-dose IV steroids and orbital decompression if not improving. Rehabilitative surgery (decompression, strabismus, then eyelid) is done in the inactive phase.
det.prognosis: Most cases are mild and self-limiting; a minority develop severe or sight-threatening disease.
pearls: Lid retraction, not ptosis — ptosis in a thyroid patient suggests coexisting myasthenia.
Restricted upgaze with a big inferior rectus on CT = thyroid eye disease.
Colour vision loss means optic nerve compression — urgent treatment.
det.thd: โรคตาจากไทรอยด์เกิดจากภูมิต้านทานต่อ TSH receptor บนเซลล์ในเบ้าตา ทำให้กล้ามเนื้อตาและไขมันหลังลูกตาบวม มักพบร่วมกับ Graves disease และสูบบุหรี่ทำให้แย่ลง อาการคือหนังตาดึงรั้ง ตาโปน ตาแดงเคือง และเห็นภาพซ้อนเพราะกล้ามเนื้อตา inferior และ medial rectus บวมแข็ง ภาวะอันตรายคือ optic nerve ถูกกดทำให้การมองเห็นและการมองสีลดลง รักษาโดยเลิกบุหรี่ คุมไทรอยด์ ให้สเตียรอยด์ทางหลอดเลือดในระยะ active และผ่าตัดลดความดันในเบ้าตาเมื่อจำเป็น

name: Tetanus
formal: Toxin-mediated disorder in which tetanospasmin from Clostridium tetani, entering through a wound, blocks inhibitory interneurons in the spinal cord and brainstem, producing generalized rigidity, painful reflex spasms and autonomic instability with a clear sensorium.
simple: A germ from a dirty wound makes a toxin that stops the brakes on muscles, so the jaw locks and the body goes into painful stiff spasms while the person stays awake.
th: บาดทะยัก — ขากรรไกรแข็ง (trismus) หน้ายิ้มเกร็ง หลังแอ่น เกร็งกระตุกเมื่อถูกกระตุ้น รู้สึกตัวดี
feat: Trismus is usually the first sign, then neck and trunk rigidity and opisthotonus
Risus sardonicus; spasms provoked by touch or noise, with laryngospasm risk
Autonomic storms: labile blood pressure, tachycardia, sweating
Wound or injection site 1–3 weeks earlier; incomplete vaccination
inv: Clinical diagnosis; spatula test (biting the spatula instead of a gag reflex)
Exclude strychnine poisoning, dystonic drug reaction, hypocalcaemia

case.story: Stepped on a rusty nail 10 days ago; for 2 days cannot open his mouth fully, then neck stiffness and painful back arching when the ward door bangs.
case.exam: Fixed grin, board-like abdomen, opisthotonic spasms on touch, alert and oriented, pulse 128 with swinging blood pressure.
case.tests: Spatula test positive; calcium normal; no history of tetanus vaccination.
case.q: What are the immediate priorities?
case.a: Protect the airway (spasms can cause laryngospasm), give human tetanus immunoglobulin, debride the wound, start metronidazole, control spasms with benzodiazepines (± magnesium) in a quiet ICU, and vaccinate later.

ddx.pt: Slowly evolving, jaw spared, anti-GAD positive, no wound
Inconsistent posturing, no autonomic instability or wound

aN: lockjaw | clostridium tetani | generalized tetanus | cephalic tetanus | neonatal tetanus

det.patho: Spores of Clostridium tetani enter through a wound, germinate in low-oxygen tissue and release tetanospasmin, which travels retrogradely along motor axons to the spinal cord and brainstem. There it cleaves synaptobrevin in inhibitory interneurons, blocking release of glycine and GABA, so motor neurons and sympathetic neurons fire unchecked. Neonatal tetanus from umbilical stump contamination remains important where maternal vaccination is incomplete.
det.clinical: After an incubation of about 3–21 days, trismus (lockjaw) is typically first, followed by risus sardonicus, dysphagia, neck and trunk rigidity, board-like abdomen and opisthotonus. Painful generalised spasms are triggered by touch, noise or light, threatening laryngospasm and respiratory failure, while consciousness remains clear. Autonomic instability, peaking in the second week, causes labile BP, arrhythmia, hyperpyrexia and sweating. Localised and cephalic forms (with facial palsy after head wounds) also occur.
det.diagnosis: The diagnosis is clinical; there is no confirmatory blood test, and wound cultures are neither sensitive nor specific. A positive spatula test (reflex biting rather than gagging when the posterior pharynx is touched) is useful. Exclude strychnine poisoning, dystonic reactions to antipsychotics or antiemetics, hypocalcaemic tetany, meningitis, dental abscess causing trismus and stiff-person syndrome.
det.treatment: Give human tetanus immunoglobulin promptly to neutralise unbound toxin, debride the wound and start metronidazole. Nurse in a quiet, dark ICU setting; control spasms with benzodiazepines and IV magnesium sulfate, adding neuromuscular blockade with ventilation when needed. Secure the airway early (often tracheostomy). Manage autonomic storms with magnesium and short-acting agents, avoiding unopposed beta-blockade. Disease does not confer immunity, so complete active vaccination with tetanus toxoid.
det.prognosis: Mortality varies widely with access to intensive care; recovery takes several weeks as new nerve terminals form, and short incubation predicts more severe disease.
pearls: Trismus with a clear sensorium and a recent wound = tetanus.
Having tetanus does not immunise you — vaccinate after recovery.
In ventilated patients, autonomic storms account for most deaths.
det.thd: บาดทะยักเกิดจากสารพิษ tetanospasmin ของเชื้อ Clostridium tetani ที่เข้าทางบาดแผล แล้ววิ่งย้อนตามเส้นประสาทไปยับยั้งเซลล์ประสาทยับยั้ง (glycine และ GABA) ในไขสันหลังและก้านสมอง ทำให้กล้ามเนื้อเกร็ง อาการแรกมักเป็นขากรรไกรแข็ง ตามด้วยหน้ายิ้มเกร็ง หลังแอ่น และเกร็งกระตุกเมื่อถูกกระตุ้น ขณะที่ผู้ป่วยรู้สึกตัวดี วินิจฉัยทางคลินิก รักษาด้วย tetanus immunoglobulin ทำแผล ให้ metronidazole คุมการเกร็งด้วย benzodiazepine และ magnesium ดูแลใน ICU และฉีดวัคซีนให้ครบหลังหาย

name: Anti-neurofascin-155 nodopathy
formal: Paranodal autoimmune neuropathy with IgG4 antibodies to neurofascin-155, presenting in younger adults as a severe distal, motor-predominant CIDP-like syndrome with sensory ataxia and tremor, very high CSF protein, root hypertrophy and poor IVIG response.
simple: An antibody-driven nerve disease in young adults that looks like severe CIDP, with shaky hands and poor balance, and usually needs rituximab rather than IVIG.
th: nodopathy จากแอนติบอดี NF155 — คนอายุน้อย อ่อนแรงปลายแขนขา เดินเซ มือสั่น โปรตีนในน้ำไขสันหลังสูงมาก IVIG ไม่ค่อยได้ผล
feat: Young onset; distal-predominant weakness with sensory ataxia
Low-frequency, disabling action tremor
Markedly raised CSF protein and enlarged spinal roots
Occasional central demyelination (combined central and peripheral demyelination)
inv: Anti-NF155 IgG (subclass IgG4) by cell-based assay
NCS: strikingly long distal motor and F-wave latencies
MRI roots/plexus; MRI brain if central symptoms

case.story: Over 4 months, weak feet, unsteady walking and a tremor that makes writing difficult; two courses of IVIG did not help.
case.exam: Distal weakness MRC 3/5, areflexia, sensory ataxia, coarse postural and action tremor.
case.tests: CSF protein 2.8 g/L; very prolonged distal motor latencies; MRI: thick lumbosacral roots; anti-NF155 IgG4 positive.
case.q: What treatment change is most likely to help?
case.a: Escalate to rituximab (plasma exchange for faster control); IgG4 antibodies respond poorly to IVIG.

ddx.pt: Older patients, early axon loss, nephrotic syndrome; tremor less typical
Antibody negative and usually responds to IVIG
Tremor without neuropathy, weakness or areflexia

aN: nf155 | anti nf155 | neurofascin 155 | nf155 cidp | nf155 antibody neuropathy

det.patho: IgG4 antibodies bind neurofascin-155, the glial anchor of the paranodal junction, and prevent it from pairing with the axonal contactin-1/Caspr1 complex. The septate-like junctions detach, ion channels drift out of position and conduction slows or fails. NF155 is also expressed by oligodendrocytes, which may explain the occasional central demyelinating lesions. There is a reported association with HLA-DRB1*15 alleles.
det.clinical: Typical patients are teenagers or young adults with a subacute-to-chronic, distal-predominant sensorimotor neuropathy that becomes severe. A coarse, low-frequency action or intention tremor and sensory ataxia out of proportion to proprioceptive loss are characteristic, possibly reflecting cerebellar-input dysfunction. Some develop cranial nerve palsies, papilloedema from very high CSF protein, or CNS demyelination (CCPD). The disorder tends to keep progressing despite repeated IVIG courses.
det.diagnosis: Confirm anti-NF155 IgG on a cell-based assay and verify subclass IgG4; low-titre or ELISA-only positives need confirmation because false positives occur. Nerve conduction shows strikingly prolonged distal motor and F-wave latencies with slowed velocities. CSF protein is usually very high and spinal MRI shows hypertrophic, sometimes enhancing, roots and plexuses. MRI brain is advised if there are central symptoms. Exclude CMT (family history, uniform slowing) and POEMS (VEGF, lambda paraprotein).
det.treatment: Rituximab is the treatment of choice and can produce durable remission, sometimes with clear antibody clearance. Plasma exchange and corticosteroids give partial short-term benefit and are used as bridging therapy. IVIG generally gives little or transient benefit. Tremor may improve along with the neuropathy; symptomatic tremor drugs add little. Physiotherapy and fall prevention address the ataxia.
det.prognosis: Outcome is good when rituximab is started before extensive axonal loss; delayed treatment leaves fixed deficits. Relapses after B-cell repopulation can occur and respond to retreatment.
pearls: Young adult + CIDP picture + tremor + huge roots + IVIG failure = test for NF155.
CSF protein can be high enough to cause raised intracranial pressure and papilloedema.
Look for central lesions — NF155 is a recognised cause of combined central and peripheral demyelination.
det.thd: โรคนี้เกิดจากแอนติบอดี IgG4 ต่อ neurofascin-155 ซึ่งเป็นโปรตีนยึดเปลือกปลอกประสาทเข้ากับแอกซอนที่ paranode พบในคนอายุน้อย อาการคล้าย CIDP รุนแรง มีอ่อนแรงปลายแขนขา เดินเซ และมือสั่นแบบหยาบ ตรวจพบโปรตีนใน CSF สูงมาก รากประสาทโตใน MRI และ distal latency ยาวมาก การวินิจฉัยยืนยันด้วย cell-based assay ส่วนการรักษาที่ได้ผลดีคือ rituximab เพราะ IVIG มักไม่ได้ผล

name: Anti-contactin-1 nodopathy
formal: Paranodal autoimmune neuropathy with antibodies (mainly IgG4) to contactin-1, typically in older adults, with rapid motor-predominant progression, sensory ataxia, early axonal loss, IVIG resistance and an association with membranous nephropathy.
simple: An antibody-driven nerve disease of older adults that worsens quickly, causes weakness and poor balance, damages nerve fibres early, may come with kidney protein loss, and responds poorly to IVIG.
th: nodopathy จากแอนติบอดี contactin-1 — ผู้สูงอายุ แย่ลงเร็ว แอกซอนเสียเร็ว อาจมีโปรตีนรั่วในปัสสาวะ (nephrotic) IVIG ไม่ได้ผล
feat: Older age at onset and a fast, severe course
Motor-predominant weakness with sensory ataxia
Early low motor amplitudes (axon loss)
Oedema and proteinuria from membranous nephropathy
inv: Anti-CNTN1 IgG with subclass
Urinalysis and urine protein quantification
NCS: low CMAPs plus demyelinating features

case.story: Eight weeks of rapidly worsening weakness and unsteadiness; her ankles have also become swollen. IVIG in week 3 made no difference.
case.exam: Distal > proximal weakness MRC 3/5, absent reflexes, positive Romberg, pitting oedema.
case.tests: Urine protein 5 g/day, low albumin; NCS: reduced CMAPs with slowed conduction; anti-CNTN1 positive.
case.q: Which non-neurological finding links the two problems?
case.a: Membranous nephropathy causing nephrotic syndrome — reported with contactin-1 (and pan-neurofascin) antibodies.

ddx.pt: Younger patients with prominent tremor and root hypertrophy
Reaches nadir within 4 weeks; usually IVIG-responsive
Painful small-fibre and autonomic neuropathy with nephrotic syndrome; amyloid on fat biopsy

aN: cntn1 | anti cntn1 | contactin 1 | contactin 1 antibody neuropathy | neuro renal syndrome

det.patho: Antibodies against contactin-1, the axonal partner of neurofascin-155 at the paranode, detach the axo-glial junction. IgG4 dominates in the chronic phase, but IgG3 (complement-fixing) may be present early, which may explain the acute onset in some patients. Axonal degeneration appears early, which distinguishes it from purely demyelinating disease. Contactin-1 is also present in kidney podocytes, and immune complexes may underlie the associated membranous nephropathy.
det.clinical: Patients are usually over 50 and develop weakness and sensory ataxia over weeks, sometimes acute enough to be called GBS. Pain, tremor and cranial nerve involvement occur but are less defining than in NF155 disease. Oedema, frothy urine or hypoalbuminaemia should be actively sought because the renal disease may be the first clue. Without targeted treatment the course is relentless and disability accumulates quickly.
det.diagnosis: Anti-CNTN1 IgG on a cell-based assay, with subclass, confirms the diagnosis; some cases have antibodies to the CNTN1/Caspr1 complex only. Nerve studies combine demyelinating features with early, marked reduction of motor amplitudes. CSF protein is high. Quantify proteinuria and consider renal biopsy if nephrotic. Exclude AL amyloidosis and POEMS, which also join neuropathy with systemic features.
det.treatment: Rituximab is the most consistently effective therapy and often improves both the neuropathy and the nephropathy. Corticosteroids and plasma exchange are used to gain early control. IVIG is usually ineffective, especially in IgG4-dominant cases. Renal management (ACE inhibition, diuretics, anticoagulation when indicated) runs in parallel with nephrology input.
det.prognosis: Response to rituximab can be good, but the early axonal loss means recovery is often incomplete and slower than in pure demyelination.
pearls: Neuropathy plus nephrotic syndrome: think CNTN1, pan-NF, AL amyloid and POEMS.
Low CMAPs early on suggest axonal damage and argue for urgent B-cell therapy.
det.thd: Nodopathy จากแอนติบอดีต่อ contactin-1 มักพบในผู้สูงอายุ อาการอ่อนแรงและเดินเซแย่ลงเร็วภายในไม่กี่สัปดาห์ แอกซอนเสียตั้งแต่ระยะแรกจึงพบ CMAP ต่ำ และอาจมีโรคไต membranous nephropathy ทำให้บวมและมีโปรตีนรั่วในปัสสาวะ ยืนยันด้วยการตรวจแอนติบอดี anti-CNTN1 ร่วมกับ subclass IVIG มักไม่ได้ผล ควรใช้ rituximab ร่วมกับสเตียรอยด์หรือ plasma exchange และดูแลไตร่วมกับอายุรแพทย์โรคไต

name: Pan-neurofascin nodopathy
formal: Severe nodo-paranodopathy with antibodies binding neurofascin-155 as well as neurofascin-186, presenting acutely like GBS with tetraplegia, cranial neuropathies, respiratory and autonomic failure; associated with nephrotic syndrome and haematological malignancy, partial response to IVIG/plasma exchange and better response to rituximab.
simple: A rare, very severe antibody attack on nerve junctions that looks like the worst form of GBS — paralysis, breathing failure and face weakness — and often needs rituximab.
th: nodopathy จากแอนติบอดีต่อ neurofascin ทั้งสองชนิด — อาการเหมือน GBS รุนแรงมาก อัมพาตทั้งตัว หายใจไม่ได้ อาจสัมพันธ์มะเร็งเม็ดเลือด
feat: Rapid tetraparesis with areflexia
Cranial nerve palsies, ventilatory failure, dysautonomia
Associated nephrotic syndrome or lymphoma/leukaemia/myeloma
inv: Anti-NF155/NF186 antibodies with subclass (IgG1/3 or IgG4)
Screen for haematological malignancy and proteinuria

case.story: Ten days of rapidly ascending weakness, facial weakness and difficulty swallowing; intubated on day 9.
case.exam: Flaccid tetraplegia, areflexia, bilateral facial palsy, labile BP and heart rate.
case.tests: Treated as GBS with IVIG and plasma exchange with little change; nephrotic-range proteinuria; antibodies to both NF155 and NF186.
case.q: What clues argued against ordinary GBS?
case.a: Extreme severity with dysautonomia, poor response to IVIG/plasma exchange, nephrotic syndrome and a haematological malignancy.

ddx.pt: Usually responds to IVIG/PLEX; antibody panel negative
Pure motor after diarrhoea with ganglioside antibodies, no nephrotic syndrome

aN: pan nf | pan neurofascin | nf155 nf186 | anti pan neurofascin

det.patho: Antibodies recognise an epitope common to both neurofascin isoforms, so they attack the paranode (NF155) and the node itself (NF186). Loss of nodal sodium-channel clustering causes abrupt, widespread conduction failure. Subclasses vary: IgG3/IgG1 forms are complement-fixing and acutely destructive, whereas IgG4 forms behave more chronically. Haematological malignancy and membranous nephropathy are recurring associations.
det.clinical: The onset is acute or subacute with tetraplegia, areflexia, facial and bulbar palsies, ophthalmoplegia, ventilatory failure and dysautonomia — a picture resembling the most severe GBS or even a locked-in state. Some patients become nearly unresponsive to nerve stimulation. Proteinuria, lymphadenopathy or abnormal blood counts point to the associations. Prolonged ICU stay is common.
det.diagnosis: Antibodies to NF155 and NF186 together on cell-based assays, with subclass, establish the diagnosis. Nerve conduction may show inexcitable nerves or diffuse conduction failure. Screen urine protein and do a haematological work-up including immunofixation, imaging and marrow when indicated. Distinguish from GBS by the lack of response to standard therapy and the antibody result.
det.treatment: Intensive care support with early ventilation and autonomic monitoring is the priority. Plasma exchange and IVIG may help, particularly IgG3 forms, but rituximab (often with steroids) is needed for sustained recovery. Treat any associated lymphoma, leukaemia or myeloma. Long rehabilitation is usually required.
det.prognosis: Mortality and residual disability are higher than in typical GBS, yet substantial recovery has been reported after B-cell depletion, even after prolonged paralysis.
pearls: A GBS patient who becomes almost completely de-efferented and does not respond to IVIG should be tested for pan-neurofascin antibodies.
Inexcitable nerves here may still recover because the problem can be functional nodal failure.
det.thd: โรคนี้เกิดจากแอนติบอดีที่จับ neurofascin ทั้งชนิด 155 และ 186 จึงทำลายทั้ง node และ paranode อาการเหมือน GBS ที่รุนแรงที่สุด คือ อัมพาตทั้งตัว เส้นประสาทสมองเสีย หายใจเองไม่ได้ และระบบประสาทอัตโนมัติแปรปรวน อาจพบร่วมกับโรคไตหรือมะเร็งเม็ดเลือด การรักษาต้องดูแลใน ICU ร่วมกับ plasma exchange หรือ IVIG และมักต้องใช้ rituximab จึงจะฟื้นตัวได้

name: Combined central and peripheral demyelination (CCPD)
formal: Coexistence of CNS demyelination (optic neuritis, brain or spinal cord lesions) with a CIDP-like demyelinating neuropathy; a subset has neurofascin-155 antibodies.
simple: A rare condition in which the protective coating of nerves is damaged both in the brain or spinal cord and in the limb nerves at the same time.
th: ปลอกประสาทเสียทั้งในสมอง/ไขสันหลังและเส้นประสาทส่วนปลายพร้อมกัน — บางรายพบแอนติบอดี NF155
feat: Optic neuritis, myelitis or brain lesions plus areflexic neuropathy
Raised CSF protein
inv: MRI brain/spine plus NCS
Anti-NF155, AQP4 and MOG antibodies

case.story: Painful blurred vision in the left eye a year ago; now numb, weak legs over 3 months.
case.exam: Left optic pallor, distal leg weakness, absent reflexes, reduced vibration, mildly brisk jaw jerk.
case.tests: MRI: periventricular lesions and a cervical cord lesion; NCS: demyelinating polyneuropathy; anti-NF155 positive.
case.q: Which single test explains both the central and the peripheral findings?
case.a: Anti-neurofascin-155 antibodies — neurofascin is found at CNS and PNS paranodes.

ddx.pt: Peripheral nerves are normal
No CNS lesions

nN: combined central and peripheral demyelination ccpd
aN: ccpd | combined central and peripheral demyelination | combined central peripheral demyelination

det.patho: CCPD is a heterogeneous syndrome in which an immune process damages myelin in both the central and the peripheral nervous system. Some patients have antibodies to neurofascin-155, which is found in both oligodendrocyte and Schwann cell paranodes; others are seronegative or have MOG-associated disease with a coexisting neuropathy. It is uncommon and was described mainly in Japanese cohorts.
det.clinical: Patients present with features of both compartments: optic neuritis, myelitis, brainstem signs or brain white-matter lesions together with a CIDP-like, areflexic sensorimotor neuropathy. The two may appear together or years apart. The course can be monophasic, relapsing or progressive.
det.diagnosis: Diagnosis requires imaging or evoked-potential evidence of CNS demyelination plus electrophysiological evidence of peripheral demyelination. Test for NF155, AQP4 and MOG antibodies and check CSF protein and oligoclonal bands. Exclude mimics such as leukodystrophies (metachromatic leukodystrophy, Krabbe), mitochondrial disease, vitamin B12 deficiency and POEMS.
det.treatment: Corticosteroids, IVIG and plasma exchange are used as for CIDP or acute CNS demyelination. NF155-positive patients usually need rituximab. Some MS disease-modifying drugs may worsen peripheral demyelination, so choices should be made with care.
det.prognosis: Variable; many patients respond partly to immunotherapy, but relapses and residual disability are common.
pearls: A patient with 'MS' and absent reflexes deserves nerve conduction studies.
Inherited leukodystrophies also affect both CNS and PNS myelin — check before calling it immune.
det.thd: CCPD คือภาวะที่ปลอกประสาทถูกทำลายทั้งในสมองหรือไขสันหลัง และในเส้นประสาทส่วนปลายพร้อมกัน ผู้ป่วยอาจมี optic neuritis, myelitis หรือรอยโรคในสมอง ร่วมกับอาการแบบ CIDP เช่น ชาและรีเฟล็กซ์หาย บางรายพบแอนติบอดี NF155 การวินิจฉัยใช้ MRI ร่วมกับการตรวจไฟฟ้าเส้นประสาท และต้องแยกโรคพันธุกรรม leukodystrophy การรักษาใช้สเตียรอยด์ IVIG หรือ plasma exchange และ rituximab ในรายที่มี NF155

name: Anti-MAG neuropathy
formal: IgM paraproteinaemic neuropathy with antibodies against myelin-associated glycoprotein, producing a slowly progressive distal, sensory-predominant demyelinating (DADS) neuropathy with sensory ataxia, tremor and disproportionately prolonged distal motor latencies.
simple: A slowly worsening nerve disease in older adults caused by an IgM antibody against nerve insulation, mainly causing numb feet, poor balance and shaky hands with little weakness.
th: เส้นประสาทเสื่อมจาก IgM ต่อ MAG — ชาปลายเท้า เดินเซ มือสั่น อ่อนแรงน้อย ดำเนินโรคช้ามาก
feat: Older men more often; progression over years
Distal sensory loss with sensory ataxia; little weakness
Postural/action tremor
Distal demyelinating pattern (very prolonged distal latencies)
inv: IgM paraprotein on immunofixation; anti-MAG antibody titre
NCS: distal accentuated slowing (low terminal latency index)
Haematology review for Waldenström macroglobulinaemia/lymphoma

case.story: Five years of numb, tingling feet; now sways in the shower when he closes his eyes and his handwriting is shaky.
case.exam: Reduced vibration and joint position in the feet, positive Romberg, mild toe weakness, absent ankle jerks, fine action tremor.
case.tests: IgM-kappa paraprotein; anti-MAG strongly positive; NCS: very prolonged distal motor latencies.
case.q: Which first-line immunotherapy is most often tried, and what is the warning?
case.a: Rituximab is commonly used for disabling disease; IgM can transiently rise after it, and some patients worsen, especially with very high IgM.

read.where: Chapter 52 DADS neuropathy, pp. 805–810; Chapter 53 Paraproteinemic neuropathies, pp. 811–826

ddx.pt: Proximal weakness, uniform/proximal slowing, responds to IVIG/steroids
Younger, rapid, severe motor weakness; no IgM paraprotein
Ophthalmoplegia, cold agglutinins and disialosyl antibodies
Same pattern — anti-MAG positive DADS is this disease; anti-MAG negative DADS behaves more like CIDP

aN: anti mag | mag neuropathy | igm anti mag | dads m | myelin associated glycoprotein neuropathy

det.patho: IgM antibodies bind myelin-associated glycoprotein (and related glycolipids such as SGPG) in peripheral myelin, deposit with complement and cause widening of the myelin lamellae, especially in distal nerve segments. This explains the disproportionate distal slowing. Roughly half of patients with IgM-MGUS neuropathy carry anti-MAG antibodies, and a minority have underlying Waldenström macroglobulinaemia. It mostly affects men over 60.
det.clinical: Numbness and tingling start in the feet and ascend very slowly over years; balance worsens, especially in the dark, and a postural or action tremor of the hands is frequent. Distal weakness appears late and is usually mild. Most patients remain ambulant for many years, but some become significantly disabled by ataxia.
det.diagnosis: Look for an IgM paraprotein (usually kappa) on immunofixation and measure anti-MAG titre; high titres are strongly supportive. NCS shows distal-accentuated demyelination with markedly prolonged distal motor latencies and a reduced terminal latency index. Refer to haematology to exclude Waldenström macroglobulinaemia or lymphoma. Nerve biopsy is rarely needed but shows widely spaced myelin with IgM deposits.
det.treatment: Treatment is reserved for disabling or progressive disease. Rituximab is the most used agent; randomised trials missed their primary endpoints but some patients clearly improve, and a transient IgM flare after the first dose can worsen symptoms. IVIG gives short-lived benefit in a few, and steroids are generally ineffective. BTK inhibitors and other haematology-directed regimens are options under study, especially if there is an underlying lymphoma.
det.prognosis: Progression is slow and life expectancy is usually normal unless a lymphoproliferative disease develops; many patients accumulate moderate disability over a decade or more.
pearls: Elderly man + sensory ataxia + tremor + IgM kappa + very long distal latencies = anti-MAG neuropathy.
Do not expect CIDP-like steroid responsiveness — anti-MAG disease rarely responds.
Check IgM level before rituximab; very high IgM raises the risk of a flare.
det.thd: Anti-MAG neuropathy เกิดจาก IgM paraprotein ที่จับโปรตีน MAG บนปลอกประสาท ทำให้ปลอกประสาทส่วนปลายเสียมากกว่าส่วนต้น มักพบในชายสูงอายุ อาการชาเท้าค่อยๆ ขึ้นมาเป็นปี เดินเซในที่มืด และมือสั่น แต่อ่อนแรงน้อย การตรวจพบ IgM kappa ระดับ anti-MAG สูง และ distal motor latency ยาวมาก ต้องส่งตรวจหา Waldenström การรักษาใช้ rituximab ในรายที่พิการมากขึ้น ส่วนสเตียรอยด์มักไม่ได้ผล

name: CANOMAD syndrome
formal: Chronic ataxic neuropathy with ophthalmoplegia, IgM M-protein, cold agglutinins and disialosyl ganglioside antibodies (GD1b, GQ1b); a chronic, paraprotein-associated counterpart of Miller Fisher syndrome with severe sensory ataxia and relative sparing of strength.
simple: A rare, long-lasting nerve disease with an IgM blood protein that causes very poor balance and eye-movement problems while strength stays fairly normal.
th: เส้นประสาทเสื่อมเรื้อรังเดินเซมาก กลอกตาผิดปกติ ร่วมกับ IgM paraprotein และ cold agglutinin — เหมือน Miller Fisher แบบเรื้อรัง
feat: Profound sensory ataxia with areflexia
Fluctuating or fixed ophthalmoplegia; may have bulbar weakness
Strength relatively preserved
inv: IgM paraprotein, cold agglutinins, anti-GD1b/GQ1b IgM

read.where: Ataxic sensory neuropathy with GD1b antibodies (CANOMAD)

case.story: Three years of worsening imbalance; episodes of double vision; his fingers go white in the cold.
case.exam: Severe sensory ataxia, areflexia, partial bilateral ophthalmoplegia, near-normal strength.
case.tests: IgM-kappa paraprotein; cold agglutinins; IgM anti-GD1b and anti-GQ1b.
case.q: Which acute syndrome does this resemble, and how does it differ?
case.a: Miller Fisher syndrome — but CANOMAD is chronic and driven by an IgM paraprotein.

ddx.pt: Acute, monophasic, IgG anti-GQ1b, no paraprotein
No ophthalmoplegia; anti-MAG positive

aN: canomad | canda | chronic ataxic neuropathy disialosyl antibodies

det.patho: An IgM paraprotein with activity against disialosyl gangliosides (GD1b, GQ1b, GD3, GT1b) binds dorsal root ganglion neurons, sensory nerve fibres and oculomotor nerves. The same IgM often behaves as a cold agglutinin. It can be regarded as a chronic IgM counterpart of the acute IgG anti-GQ1b disorders such as Miller Fisher syndrome.
det.clinical: Patients, usually middle-aged or older, develop severe sensory ataxia with areflexia while strength is largely preserved. Ophthalmoplegia may be fixed or relapsing-remitting, and some have bulbar or facial weakness. CANDA is the term for cases without ophthalmoplegia. The course is chronic, sometimes with stepwise exacerbations.
det.diagnosis: Look for an IgM paraprotein with anti-disialosyl antibodies; cold agglutinins are found in many, but not all. NCS shows a sensory neuronopathy-like or mixed demyelinating-axonal pattern. Haematological evaluation is needed to exclude Waldenström macroglobulinaemia or lymphoma. Distinguish from anti-MAG neuropathy, sensory neuronopathies (Sjögren, paraneoplastic) and Miller Fisher syndrome.
det.treatment: IVIG gives partial or transient improvement in many patients and is often used first. Rituximab, alone or with chemotherapy, can be effective, particularly when there is an underlying lymphoproliferative disorder. Steroids are generally of little value. Supportive measures address ataxia and diplopia.
det.prognosis: The disorder tends to be chronic with persistent ataxia, but some patients stabilise or improve with treatment.
pearls: Chronic ataxia + ophthalmoplegia + IgM band = CANOMAD; ask the lab to check cold agglutinins.
Strength is relatively spared despite profound ataxia.
det.thd: CANOMAD เป็นโรคเส้นประสาทเรื้อรังที่สัมพันธ์กับ IgM paraprotein ซึ่งทำหน้าที่เป็นแอนติบอดีต่อ ganglioside กลุ่ม disialosyl เช่น GD1b และ GQ1b ผู้ป่วยเดินเซมาก รีเฟล็กซ์หาย และกลอกตาผิดปกติ แต่กำลังกล้ามเนื้อค่อนข้างดี มักพบ cold agglutinin ร่วม คล้าย Miller Fisher แบบเรื้อรัง การรักษาใช้ IVIG หรือ rituximab และต้องตรวจหาโรคมะเร็งต่อมน้ำเหลือง

name: Cryoglobulinaemic neuropathy
formal: Painful axonal neuropathy — usually mononeuritis multiplex or an asymmetric distal pattern — caused by vasculitis of nerve vessels in cryoglobulinaemia, most often mixed cryoglobulinaemia related to hepatitis C.
simple: Painful nerve damage, often affecting one nerve after another, from inflamed small blood vessels in people whose blood contains proteins that clump in the cold (often linked to hepatitis C).
th: เส้นประสาทเสียจากหลอดเลือดอักเสบในภาวะ cryoglobulin — ปวดมาก เส้นประสาทเสียทีละเส้น มักสัมพันธ์ไวรัสตับอักเสบซี
feat: Painful, often asymmetric sensory > motor neuropathy; may be mononeuritis multiplex
Purpura of the legs, arthralgia, glomerulonephritis, Raynaud phenomenon
Hepatitis C is the commonest trigger
inv: Cryoglobulins (sample kept warm), complement C4 (low), rheumatoid factor
Hepatitis C serology/RNA
Nerve (± muscle) biopsy for vasculitis

read.where: บทที่ 4 Vasculitic neuropathy หน้า 53–68 (การจำแนก ตารางที่ 4.1 หน้า 53; เกณฑ์ ตารางที่ 4.2 หน้า 56; การรักษา ตารางที่ 4.4 หน้า 61)

case.story: Burning pain in the left foot, then a few weeks later right wrist drop; purple spots appear on her shins.
case.exam: Palpable purpura on the legs, left sural sensory loss, right radial nerve palsy.
case.tests: Cryoglobulins positive, C4 very low, rheumatoid factor positive; sural nerve biopsy: vasculitis.
case.q: What pattern of neuropathy is this?
case.a: Mononeuritis multiplex from vasculitis — treat the hepatitis C and the vasculitis.

ddx.pt: Other systemic vasculitides (ANCA, PAN) without cryoglobulins
Symmetric length-dependent, no purpura

aN: cryoglobulinemic neuropathy | cryoglobulinemic vasculitis neuropathy | mixed cryoglobulinemia neuropathy

det.patho: Cryoglobulins are immunoglobulins that precipitate in the cold. In mixed cryoglobulinaemia (types II and III), immune complexes containing IgM with rheumatoid factor activity and polyclonal IgG deposit in small vessel walls, activate complement and cause vasculitis of the vasa nervorum, leading to ischaemic axonal injury. Chronic hepatitis C is the commonest driver; others include Sjögren syndrome, lupus, hepatitis B, HIV and B-cell lymphoma. Type I (single monoclonal) cryoglobulins more often cause occlusion and hyperviscosity.
det.clinical: The neuropathy is usually a painful, sensory-predominant distal polyneuropathy, sometimes asymmetric, or a mononeuritis multiplex with stepwise nerve palsies. Palpable purpura of the legs, arthralgia, weakness and fatigue, Raynaud phenomenon, skin ulcers and glomerulonephritis form the systemic picture. Symptoms can worsen in the cold.
det.diagnosis: Cryoglobulin testing requires blood collection and transport at 37 °C; mishandling causes false negatives. Low C4, positive rheumatoid factor and hepatitis C serology/RNA support the diagnosis. NCS show axonal, often asymmetric changes. Nerve and muscle biopsy can demonstrate vasculitis. Look for kidney disease (urinalysis, creatinine) and lymphoma.
det.treatment: In hepatitis C-related disease, direct-acting antiviral therapy is the foundation and may control the vasculitis. Rituximab is the main immunosuppressive option for active or severe vasculitis, with corticosteroids for short-term control. Plasma exchange is used for life- or organ-threatening disease. Neuropathic pain treatment and cold avoidance are supportive measures.
det.prognosis: Neuropathy often stabilises with antiviral and B-cell therapy, but axonal damage recovers slowly and incompletely; renal involvement and lymphoma determine long-term outcome.
pearls: Purpura + neuropathy + low C4 = check cryoglobulins and hepatitis C.
A negative cryoglobulin test is unreliable unless the sample was kept warm.
det.thd: Cryoglobulinaemic neuropathy เกิดจากโปรตีน cryoglobulin ที่ตกตะกอนในอุณหภูมิเย็น ไปสะสมที่ผนังหลอดเลือดเล็กของเส้นประสาทจนเกิดหลอดเลือดอักเสบ ผู้ป่วยมีอาการปวดชาปลายเท้า หรือเส้นประสาทเสียทีละเส้น ร่วมกับผื่นจ้ำเลือดที่ขา ปวดข้อ และอาจมีไตอักเสบ สาเหตุที่พบบ่อยคือไวรัสตับอักเสบซี การตรวจต้องเก็บเลือดในอุณหภูมิ 37 องศา ร่วมกับตรวจ C4 และ rheumatoid factor การรักษาคือยาต้านไวรัสตับอักเสบซี และ rituximab ในรายที่หลอดเลือดอักเสบรุนแรง

name: Waldenström macroglobulinaemia neuropathy
formal: Neuropathy in Waldenström macroglobulinaemia (IgM-secreting lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma), usually a distal sensory or sensorimotor demyelinating neuropathy (often anti-MAG), less often motor-predominant with anti-GM1 IgM, or due to hyperviscosity, amyloid or infiltration.
simple: Nerve damage in a slow blood cancer that makes large amounts of IgM antibody, usually causing numb feet and unsteady walking.
th: เส้นประสาทเสื่อมในมะเร็งต่อมน้ำเหลืองชนิดสร้าง IgM — ชาปลายเท้า เดินเซ คล้าย anti-MAG
feat: Distal sensory loss and gait unsteadiness
Systemic: anaemia, lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, hyperviscosity (headache, visual blurring, bleeding)
CNS infiltration (Bing–Neel syndrome) is a rare separate complication
inv: IgM paraprotein level, anti-MAG and anti-GM1
Bone marrow biopsy; MYD88 L265P mutation
Fundoscopy and serum viscosity if symptomatic

case.story: Gradually numb feet and unsteady gait over 2 years; recently tired, with nosebleeds and blurred vision.
case.exam: Distal sensory loss with sensory ataxia, mild toe weakness; fundi show dilated, sausage-like retinal veins.
case.tests: IgM-kappa 42 g/L; serum viscosity high; marrow: lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate; MYD88 L265P positive; anti-MAG positive.
case.q: Which finding needs urgent treatment before the neuropathy?
case.a: Hyperviscosity (nosebleeds, visual blurring, retinal vein changes) — plasma exchange, then haematological therapy.

ddx.pt: IgM MGUS without lymphoma criteria
Painful small-fibre and autonomic neuropathy

aN: waldenstrom | waldenstrom macroglobulinemia | wm neuropathy | lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma neuropathy | bing neel

det.patho: Waldenström macroglobulinaemia is a lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma secreting monoclonal IgM; the MYD88 L265P mutation is present in the great majority. Neuropathy arises mainly when the IgM has anti-MAG or anti-ganglioside activity, but it may also result from cryoglobulins, AL amyloid, hyperviscosity, or direct infiltration of nerves and roots by lymphoma cells. CNS infiltration (Bing–Neel syndrome) is a separate complication.
det.clinical: The typical pattern is a slowly progressive, distal, symmetric sensory or sensorimotor neuropathy with ataxia, similar to anti-MAG neuropathy. Painful or asymmetric neuropathy suggests amyloid, cryoglobulin or infiltration. Systemic features include fatigue, anaemia, lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, and hyperviscosity symptoms such as headache, blurred vision, epistaxis and confusion.
det.diagnosis: Diagnosis needs an IgM paraprotein with lymphoplasmacytic infiltration of the marrow; MYD88 and CXCR4 mutation testing support the diagnosis and guide therapy. Test anti-MAG and anti-ganglioside antibodies, cryoglobulins and, if indicated, fat pad for amyloid. Fundoscopy and serum viscosity are needed if hyperviscosity is suspected. MRI with contrast and CSF cytology/flow cytometry are used if Bing–Neel syndrome is possible.
det.treatment: Treatment is directed at the lymphoma when neuropathy is significant or progressive, using rituximab-based regimens (e.g. with bendamustine) or BTK inhibitors. Neurotoxic agents such as bortezomib should be used cautiously. Plasma exchange rapidly relieves symptomatic hyperviscosity. Neuropathic pain treatment and physiotherapy are supportive.
det.prognosis: Waldenström is usually indolent with long survival; the neuropathy may stabilise with treatment but complete recovery is uncommon.
pearls: An IgM neuropathy needs haematological work-up to separate IgM MGUS from Waldenström.
Hyperviscosity is an emergency treated with plasma exchange, not transfusion.
det.thd: Waldenström macroglobulinaemia เป็นมะเร็งต่อมน้ำเหลืองชนิดที่สร้าง IgM ปริมาณมาก เกือบทุกรายมีการกลายพันธุ์ MYD88 L265P เส้นประสาทเสื่อมเกิดได้หลายกลไก ที่พบบ่อยคือ IgM ทำหน้าที่เป็น anti-MAG ทำให้ชาปลายเท้าและเดินเซ นอกจากนี้อาจมีอาการเลือดหนืด เช่น ปวดศีรษะ ตามัว และเลือดกำเดาไหล การวินิจฉัยต้องตรวจไขกระดูก และตรวจแอนติบอดีที่เกี่ยวข้อง การรักษาคือยาที่มี rituximab เป็นหลัก หรือยากลุ่ม BTK inhibitor และทำ plasma exchange เมื่อเลือดหนืดมาก

name: Chronic immune sensory polyradiculopathy (CISP)
formal: Immune-mediated inflammation restricted to the preganglionic sensory roots, producing progressive sensory ataxia, paraesthesia and areflexia with normal routine nerve conduction studies; a proximal variant within the CIDP spectrum that responds to immunotherapy.
simple: An immune attack on the sensory nerve roots next to the spinal cord, causing unsteady walking and numbness, while ordinary nerve tests look normal.
th: รากประสาทรับความรู้สึกอักเสบจากภูมิคุ้มกัน — เดินเซ ชา รีเฟล็กซ์หาย แต่ตรวจคลื่นไฟฟ้าเส้นประสาทปกติ
feat: Gait ataxia, falls in the dark, positive Romberg
Areflexia with little or no weakness
Routine sensory nerve action potentials are normal (lesion is proximal to the ganglion)
inv: Somatosensory evoked potentials: delayed or absent proximal responses
MRI lumbar spine with contrast: thickened, enhancing roots; CSF protein raised

case.story: Eighteen months of unsteadiness, worse in the dark, with tingling feet.
case.exam: Absent reflexes, impaired joint position sense in toes, positive Romberg, normal strength.
case.tests: Normal sural and median SNAPs; tibial SSEPs absent; MRI: enhancing cauda equina roots; CSF protein 1.1 g/L.
case.q: Why are the nerve conduction studies normal despite sensory ataxia?
case.a: The inflammation is in the preganglionic roots — the dorsal root ganglion and distal axons are intact, so SNAPs are preserved.

ddx.pt: Ganglion damage gives absent SNAPs, often asymmetric, paraneoplastic or Sjögren
UMN signs and low B12
Lightning pains, Argyll Robertson pupils, positive syphilis serology

aN: cisp | chronic immune sensory polyradiculopathy | cismp | sensory cidp proximal

det.patho: CISP is an immune-mediated inflammatory disorder of the dorsal (sensory) roots, located on the spinal-cord side of the ganglion. Because the ganglion cell bodies and their peripheral axons are intact, distal sensory nerve conduction is preserved, while central-going proprioceptive input is blocked. It is now considered within the CIDP spectrum (EAN/PNS 2021 lists sensory-predominant and root-predominant forms), and some patients later develop motor involvement.
det.clinical: Patients present with slowly progressive gait ataxia, falls particularly in darkness, and paraesthesia in the legs, sometimes extending to the arms. Examination shows loss of vibration and joint position sense, a positive Romberg sign and absent or reduced reflexes with normal or near-normal strength. Pain is uncommon. A related entity, CISMP, includes motor root involvement.
det.diagnosis: Routine NCS are normal or nearly normal, which is the key paradox. Somatosensory evoked potentials show prolonged or absent proximal responses with preserved peripheral potentials. MRI of the lumbar spine with gadolinium shows thickened, enhancing roots or cauda equina, and CSF protein is usually elevated without pleocytosis. Exclude dorsal column disease (B12, copper, syphilis, HIV), compressive lesions, sensory neuronopathy and infiltrative or infectious root disease.
det.treatment: Immunotherapy as for CIDP is used: IVIG, corticosteroids or plasma exchange, with response tracked using objective balance and sensory measures. Many patients improve markedly. Gait rehabilitation and fall prevention are important adjuncts.
det.prognosis: Response to immunotherapy is generally good, though relapse may require maintenance therapy. Untreated disease leads to progressive disabling ataxia.
pearls: Sensory ataxia + areflexia + normal NCS: get SSEPs and contrast MRI of the roots.
Normal SNAPs point to a preganglionic lesion.
Treatable — do not dismiss as idiopathic ataxia.
det.thd: CISP เป็นการอักเสบจากภูมิคุ้มกันที่รากประสาทรับความรู้สึกก่อนถึงปมประสาท ผู้ป่วยเดินเซโดยเฉพาะในที่มืด Romberg บวก รีเฟล็กซ์หาย แต่กำลังกล้ามเนื้อปกติ จุดสำคัญคือ NCS ปกติเพราะเซลล์ในปมประสาทยังดี ต้องตรวจ SSEP, MRI กระดูกสันหลังส่วนเอวฉีดสี (รากประสาทหนาและ enhance) และ CSF protein สูง รักษาแบบ CIDP ด้วย IVIG หรือ steroid และมักตอบสนองดี

name: X-linked Charcot–Marie–Tooth disease (CMTX1)
formal: Inherited neuropathy caused by mutations in GJB1 (connexin-32), the second commonest CMT; males have a heavier disease burden than carrier females, conduction slowing is intermediate and non-uniform, and transient stroke-like CNS episodes with reversible white matter lesions can occur.
simple: A family nerve disease passed on the X chromosome, so men are worse affected; it causes weak, thin lower legs and hands and can rarely cause brief stroke-like attacks.
th: CMT ชนิดถ่ายทอดทางโครโมโซม X (ยีน GJB1) — ผู้ชายอาการหนักกว่า อาจมีอาการคล้าย stroke ชั่วคราว
feat: Distal wasting and weakness; hand muscles (especially thenar) affected early
No male-to-male transmission; carrier women milder
Transient episodes of dysarthria, ataxia or weakness, often after fever, altitude or exertion
inv: NCS: intermediate conduction velocities (30–45 m/s), non-uniform
MRI during episodes: reversible posterior white matter/splenial lesions
GJB1 genetic testing

case.story: Thin legs and clumsy hands; after a trip to high altitude he had 12 hours of slurred speech and weak legs that resolved fully. His maternal uncle 'walked on high steps'.
case.exam: Distal leg and thenar wasting, pes cavus, absent ankle jerks, mild distal sensory loss.
case.tests: Median motor velocity 36 m/s; MRI during episode: symmetric restricted diffusion in posterior white matter and splenium, resolved 2 weeks later; GJB1 variant.
case.q: Why is the stroke-like episode important to recognise?
case.a: It is transient and benign in CMTX1 — recognising it avoids unnecessary stroke or MS treatment.

ddx.pt: CMT1A: uniform slowing <38 m/s, male-to-male transmission possible
Pure motor, normal sensory studies
Persistent deficit with vascular territory lesion

nN: x linked charcot marie tooth disease cmtx1
aN: cmtx1 | x linked charcot marie tooth disease | cmtx | cmt1x | gjb1 | connexin 32 neuropathy | x linked cmt

det.patho: CMTX1 results from variants in GJB1, encoding connexin-32, a gap junction protein that links layers of the myelin sheath in Schwann cells and is also expressed by oligodendrocytes. Loss of function disrupts radial transport across myelin, causing a mixed demyelinating and axonal neuropathy. Because the gene is on the X chromosome, hemizygous males are more severely affected, and heterozygous females vary because of X-inactivation.
det.clinical: Males typically present in childhood or adolescence with distal leg weakness, foot deformities, and early involvement of intrinsic hand muscles, often with thenar more than hypothenar wasting. Sensory loss and areflexia are common, and females range from asymptomatic to mildly affected later in life. A distinctive feature is transient CNS episodes — dysarthria, ataxia, hemiparesis or weakness lasting hours to days — often triggered by fever, high altitude, hyperventilation or intense exertion. Persistent subtle CNS signs such as extensor plantars or abnormal brainstem auditory potentials can be present.
det.diagnosis: NCS show intermediate motor conduction velocities (often 30–45 m/s in males), with non-uniform slowing and greater axonal loss than CMT1A; females may have near-normal or variable values. MRI during CNS episodes shows reversible, symmetric restricted diffusion in deep and posterior white matter and the splenium. Family history without male-to-male transmission is suggestive, and GJB1 testing confirms the diagnosis, including non-coding regions if initial testing is negative.
det.treatment: Treatment is supportive: physiotherapy, orthoses, foot surgery when needed, and occupational therapy for hand weakness. Patients should be advised to avoid known triggers for CNS episodes when practical, such as rapid ascent to altitude, and recognise that episodes resolve. Genetic counselling is important because daughters of affected men are obligate carriers and sons are unaffected.
det.prognosis: Slowly progressive, with most patients remaining ambulant; CNS episodes are usually fully reversible.
pearls: Stroke-like episode in a young man with neuropathy: consider CMTX1 before thrombolysis or MS treatment.
No male-to-male transmission; intermediate conduction velocities.
Split-hand pattern with thenar wasting is common.
det.thd: CMTX1 เกิดจากยีน GJB1 (connexin-32) บนโครโมโซม X ผู้ชายจึงมีอาการมากกว่าผู้หญิง ผู้ป่วยมีขาส่วนปลายและกล้ามเนื้อมือลีบอ่อนแรง เท้าโก่ง NCS ช้าระดับกลาง (30–45 m/s) และไม่สม่ำเสมอ อาจมีอาการคล้าย stroke ชั่วคราว (พูดไม่ชัด เดินเซ อ่อนแรง) หลังไข้ ขึ้นที่สูง หรือออกแรงหนัก MRI พบรอยโรคเนื้อขาวที่หายได้ ยืนยันด้วยยีน GJB1 รักษาแบบประคับประคองและให้คำปรึกษาทางพันธุกรรม

name: Transient ischaemic attack (TIA)
formal: Brief episode of focal neurological dysfunction caused by focal brain, spinal cord or retinal ischaemia, without acute infarction on imaging; a warning of early stroke.
simple: A 'mini-stroke': stroke-like symptoms that go away by themselves, usually within minutes, but signal a high risk of a real stroke soon.
th: สมองขาดเลือดชั่วคราว — อาการเหมือนอัมพาตแต่หายเองภายในไม่นาน เป็นสัญญาณเตือนว่าอาจเกิด stroke จริงในไม่ช้า
tempoNote: Abrupt onset, resolves usually within an hour
feat: Sudden negative symptoms that resolve completely
Transient monocular blindness (amaurosis fugax) implicates the ipsilateral carotid
Risk of stroke is highest in the first 48 hours
inv: Urgent MRI with DWI (a DWI lesion reclassifies it as a minor stroke)
Carotid duplex or CTA; ECG and rhythm monitoring for AF
Glucose, lipids, HbA1c

case.story: Twice this week a 'curtain' came down over her right eye for 3 minutes and then lifted.
case.exam: Normal neurological examination today; right carotid bruit.
case.tests: MRI DWI normal; carotid duplex: 80% right internal carotid stenosis.
case.q: Where is the source and what is the next step?
case.a: Symptomatic right ICA stenosis causing amaurosis fugax — start antiplatelet and statin and refer for early carotid revascularisation.

ddx.pt: Positive spreading phenomena over minutes followed by headache
Positive jerking or tingling that marches; may be followed by Todd’s weakness
Isolated anterograde amnesia with repetitive questioning, no focal signs
Glucose low at the time of symptoms

aN: tia | transient ischemic attack | mini stroke | amaurosis fugax
